anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: Persistence stays scoped. anti_goal_violations.evidence: The Foundry read surface now performs a filesystem WRITE on every page load. micro_routes.get_foundry() calls foundry_runner.read_exhaust_progress per request (micro_routes.py:941), which runs a live single-flight probe (foundry_runner.py:250-254); SingleFlightLock.acquire (foundry_runner.py:197-201) does path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) then open(path, 'w') BEFORE the try, so a GET creates/truncates apps/backend/.data/foundry/foundry_exhaust_runner.lock. Evaluator read the code directly; audit finding B5 independently confirmed the real lock file's mtime tracks the QA browser pass (10:10), not the 07:55 CLI run. Named consequences: a GET holding LOCK_EX for microseconds can make a concurrent exhaust-CLI invocation raise ConcurrentRunnerRefused; an unwritable Foundry directory now 500s a surface that was previously write-free (it degrades honestly via foundry-panel-unavailable rather than lying); errno.EACCES is mapped to ConcurrentRunnerRefused so a permissions failure would be reported to the operator as 'Running - lock held by another invocation'. SCORED AS A LITERAL-READING VIOLATION and disclosed as such: the rail's operative intent is INTACT - no market data is recorded, no candidate is computed or evaluated, and the exhaust runner is not triggered - only the words 'are read-only' are contradicted. MINOR, never critical (no secret, paid dependency, license breach, backdoor, or fabricated data, and not goal.md's own named critical violation). UNFIXABLE INSIDE THIS ERA: the fix site is read_exhaust_progress/SingleFlightLock inside foundry_runner.py, a freeze-set member whose sha256 is pinned in the one-way epoch_open ledger row - so this is an owner disposition decision, not an iteration task.
